newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Merck, Roche AIDS drugs.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Merck, Roche AIDS drugs.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had approved two AIDS-fighting drugs for sale in the European Union.
The drugs are Crixivan, produced by Merck and Co, and Invirase, produced by Hoffman-La Roche, a unit of Roche Holding Ltd.
The products, already on the market in the United States, are known as "protease inhibitors" and block enzymes that are the key to replication of the AIDS virus.
The Commission approved the drugs following a positive recommendation from the European Medicines Evaluation Agency (EMEA) in London, Commission spokesman Jochen Kubosch told a news briefing.
The EMEA, which opened just last year, allows companies to get their drugs authorised across the EU under a centralised system rather than seeking separate approvals in each member country.

AIDS activists have criticised the Commission for taking too long to make its decision on the two new drugs. But Kubosch said the process took far less time than national procedures would have done, noting that the application for Crixivan had arrived only on March 1.
"This shows that it's much faster than the procedures in the member states," who take an average of two or three years to authorise drugs, he said.
